document.abstract: Y'CbCr color space has permeated every aspect of the video industry. It is used by most compression standards, such as JPEG and MPEG, as well as for transmission, storage, and processing. Conversions between Y'CbCr and R'G'B' color spaces are defined by several industry standards. Properties and statistics of these conversions are studied. Single- and multiple-generations of conversions are compared, considering HDTV and SDTV.

authors.bio: Victor J. Duvanenko is a hardware scientist and senior software engineer at Pinnacle Systems, where he has worked for 13 years. He has developed several generations of programmable, custom, faster-than-realtime video processing chips for SDTV and HDTV as well as a realtime video processing software library, which is highly optimized for the latest generation of processors, using their specialty SIMD-style instructions. Prior to Pinnacle, Duvanenko worked as a VLSI design engineer for Intel and Silicon Engineering. He has published 13 technical papers, presented at several conferences, and holds one patent. He has B.S. and M.S. degrees in electrical engineering from Purdue University, and North Carolina State University, respectively. Duvanenko is a member of SMPTE, IEEE, and ACM. He can be contacted at duvanenko@ieee.org .
